body.statement: Suppose \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\). The coupled-pattern handle is cardinality-minimal among schedule problems having a nontrivial pairwise rank comparison, own-treatment variation for every focal unit, and at least one potential-outcome coordinate shared by two distinct assignment scores: necessarily \(N\geq2\) and \(m\geq3\), and the handle attains \(N=2\) and \(m=3\). Its shared-coordinate equalities and the two effect-exceedance constraints connect all three assignment-specific rank comparisons, so the feasible schedule set is not a product of independent stratumwise schedule sets.
body.justification: A minimal nonseparable instance fixes the residual schedule question at the first fiber where partition and stratumwise reductions genuinely cease to apply.
body.gap: The exchangeable corner and multiple-choice-knapsack comparators factor schedule choices by a single cell or by independent strata and contain no shared-coordinate three-score pattern.
body.consumer: An exact solver can use the two-unit, three-assignment instance as its smallest coupled regression test.
